content.thinking:
I'm putting together the postmortem and noting that the deploy at 00:57 UTC on October 29 removed the month total update from record_purchase. The alert shows every shopper's total for the month is off, so I'm tracing how the purchase path relates to that.

I'm weighing whether users would have noticed anything, since the alert only says totals don't reconcile and records no customer loss. The monthly statements and the account page both read that stored month total, so I'm settling on how to describe what shoppers actually saw.

I'm laying out the causal chain now: the stored month totals disagree with purchases, because purchases since the deploy left the month total unchanged. That traces back to the revision deployed at 00:57:18 that dropped the month-total update, and I'm ruling out the earlier deploy and any flag changes, since the alert puts the first harm after that deploy.

I'm settling the root-cause step: the code that reads the month total still reads the stored field instead of summing purchases, so removing the update broke every reader that depended on it. I'm checking the chain against the purchase, deploy, and reader rows rather than the flag readings, since those are the ones that actually ran.

I'm now stating the root-cause step: the change dropped upkeep of the stored month total, while the code that shows and checks it still reads that stored figure instead of summing purchases. I'm also noting that the deriving path behaves the same way, so the flag setting doesn't change the outcome, and I'm starting to list the contributing factors, beginning with how the spend-integrity check only runs every few days.

I'm checking whether the postmortem's contributing factors hold up, starting with how the spend-integrity check only runs every few days and so caught the mismatch late. I'm also considering whether a test before the deploy could have caught the dropped month-total update, since the existing test on main pins the month addition and it would seem to fail against this revision.

I'm checking whether the tests would have caught this before the deploy, since the test file at that revision includes one that expects the month total to be added to, and the deployed record_purchase no longer does that. Nothing I've seen shows those tests were run as a gate, so I'm noting that as a possible contributing factor and planning to propose a pre-deploy check.

I'm now writing up the last two contributing factors: nobody was paged when the alert fired, so no one was there to roll back sooner, and nothing in the write path checks for a mismatch, so a check after each write or an hourly reconcile could catch it early.

I'm drafting the contributing factors now, and I'm planning to merge the cadence point into the write-path item rather than keep it separate. The readers' check is the more useful angle: the docstring says the month can be summed on demand, yet the readers still use the stored field, so I'm proposing a review step that lists a changed field's readers before merge.

I'm now sorting out the remaining contributing factors: the test file at the deployed revision includes a test expecting the month total to be added to, and I haven't seen any run of it gating the deploy, so I'll flag that as a process gap. I'm also weighing whether the rollback counts as a contributing factor, and I'm leaning toward treating it as mitigation only, since it stopped further corruption without explaining the failure.

I'm now working out the action items, starting with the repair: correcting the stored month totals for every account written since the deploy, using the repair script in PR #429 from an export taken within the same month. The purchases from October 29 to 31 no longer fall in the current month, so that cutoff needs a check. I'm also noting that the purchase path on main still moves the month total, and I'll confirm whether that stays in place.

I'm wrapping up the action items: the rollback should restore month upkeep for new purchases, since the comparison against the earlier revision included that addition. I'm also lining up the follow-ups: running the spend-integrity check more often, paging on-call for the reconcile alert, requiring the test suite to pass before a deploy, and having reviewers list the readers of any stored field a change stops writing.

I'm wrapping up the postmortem's wins and misses: the investigator traced the deployment diff, Argus held off on any change it couldn't test and recommended a rollback, and Code-Fix put forward a draft PR. I'm leaving the "what went wrong" list open for now, since nothing in what I've seen clearly belongs there beyond the contributing factors already covered.

I'm moving on to the less obvious parts of the write-up: whether the shop is actually harmed beyond the saved totals, and what the postmortem can and cannot assume about what shoppers see. I'm also starting the root-cause statement that revision 26f1d7e removed the month-total update from record_purchase.

I'm settling the root-cause statement: the change stopped updating each shopper's stored month total, while the statement, spend summary, and reconcile paths still read that stored figure rather than summing the month's purchases. I'm also checking that the deploy timing and the flag changes don't explain it, since the oldest affected purchase falls after the first purchase, and nothing in the metrics from the hour before onset points elsewhere.

I'm checking that the write-up's went-well list only names things the investigation actually did: the investigator tracing the deployment diff, Argus declining to act on an untested change and leaving the rollback to a person, and the Code-Fix Agent proposing a draft fix. I'm now looking at the remaining contributing factor, that nobody was paged when the alert fired, to see which action item addresses it.

action_items.item: After the rollback, rewrite the stored month total of every account written since the deploy so it matches its current-month purchases. Take the export in the same month as the repair.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation automatically after every deploy of io-shop, not only on its weekly schedule.
Add a check on the purchase write path that flags an account whose stored month total disagrees with its current-month purchases right after it is written.
Require any change that stops writing a stored field to list that field's readers, and to show each one moved off it, before it is merged.
Make a passing run of the io-shop test suite a required gate before any revision is deployed from the deploy/ directory.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the io-shop on-call rotation so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: The saved month totals of the shoppers checked no longer matched the purchases recorded against them. The spend-integrity check found this, not any shopper report.

Purchases recorded at the running revision were added to the account and to its lifetime total, but the stored month total was left unchanged. Both write paths in the file behave this way: record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of 4c810f22894e612ced87f5ee3f3062dfeb785050: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after the later deploy of 26f1d7e at {P2.1}.
A flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2, deployed to io-shop at {P2.1}, removed the conditional total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase. All {T10.2} replicas were running it as of {T10.1}.

The change stopped keeping the stored month total up to date, but the code that renders statements, works out monthly spend and reconciles totals still reads that stored field instead of adding up the month's purchases.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop updating each shopper's saved total for this month's spending when they bought something, but the parts of the shop that show and check that total still read the saved figure.

contributing_factors.factor: The only check seen that compares stored month totals with purchases is the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The write path itself does not notice the two drifting apart.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran soon after each deploy, or after each write, would have caught the first short total soon after the deploy instead of {alerted_after_the_onset} later, which would have shortened how long bad totals kept being written.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the deploy, no check was seen that the code still reading total_this_month_cents had been moved off it. The change says the month adds up from the purchase history, but the statement, spend-summary and reconciliation code still read the stored field.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A review that listed the readers of the dropped field would have shown them still reading it, and the change would have been held back or its readers changed first.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No test run blocking the deploy was seen. Code-Fix reports that the test file at the running revision holds a test that the month is added to the total record_purchase receives, which the deployed record_purchase no longer does.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A required test run before deploying would have stopped the revision from going out.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have done the recommended rollback once the alert fired, which would have stopped more bad totals being written sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 26f1d7e changed, which pointed straight at the removed month-total update.
Argus did not act on C1 when nothing could tell whether the action had worked, and recommended the rollback to a person instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #429.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e removed the total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase, and at that revision the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so every purchase was appended to the account while its stored month total stayed where it was. The code that shows and checks that figure (render_monthly_statement, average_spend_per_item_this_month, the_mean_purchase_this_month, reconcile_monthly_totals) still reads account.total_this_month_cents rather than adding up the month's purchases, so it gets a stale figure that falls short of what the purchases add up to.
input.still_at_risk: Until a person rolls io-shop back, every new purchase can leave another shopper's saved month total short of what they bought, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong on statements and spend summaries until someone rewrites them.
input.symptom: Shoppers' saved spend-this-month totals fell short of their actual purchases
